title: Deep learning on chest CT distinguishes COVID-19 pneumonia from influenza pneumonia
summary: A deep learning framework on chest CT was trained on 35 confirmed COVID-19 (NCP) cases plus 361 viral pneumonia patients, and validated on an external set of 57 NCP and 50 influenza pneumonia patients from eight centers. The abstract reports AUC above 0.93 and an F1 score of 0.847, versus 0.785 for specialists and 0.644 for residents. Training used only 35 NCP cases and the study is retrospective. This is the 2020-03-30 preprint version.
ai_technology: Deep learning framework (Plain and Trinary schemes) on chest CT images for classification of COVID-19 versus influenza pneumonia
organization: Ruijin Hospital, Shanghai Jiao Tong University School of Medicine

evidence.tested: External validation on 57 NCP and 50 influenza pneumonia patients from eight centers; AUC above 0.93 and F1 0.847 versus specialists 0.785 and residents 0.644.
evidence.unknown: Performance beyond the retrospective external set, effect on clinical decisions and peer-reviewed status are not established from the abstract; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Deep learning classified chest CT images to differentiate COVID-19 pneumonia from influenza pneumonia.
